name: BETA GLUCOSIDASE GAUCHER BLOOD
interpretation:
The Beta-Glucosidase Blood Test (also known as glucocerebrosidase activity test) measures the activity of the beta-glucocerebrosidase enzyme, which is deficient in individuals with Gaucher disease.

Gaucher disease is a lysosomal storage disorder caused by mutations in the GBA gene, leading to the accumulation of glucocerebroside in various organs like the liver, spleen, and bone marrow.

This test is used for:

  • Diagnosing Gaucher disease (particularly Type 1, the non-neuronopathic form)

  • Carrier screening in at-risk individuals

  • Confirming diagnosis in patients with unexplained hepatosplenomegaly, cytopenias, or bone disease

  • Supporting diagnosis before genetic confirmation

 

Condition Clinical Significance
Gaucher Disease (Type 1, 2, or 3) Enzyme activity is markedly reduced (often <15% of normal), leading to lipid accumulation in macrophages
Carrier of Gaucher Disease Enzyme activity may be mildly reduced but typically not low enough to cause disease

 

Note: Definitive diagnosis should be confirmed by GBA gene mutation analysis, especially for subtyping and prognosis.

Result -  A reduced (`17.3% mean normal ) enzyme activity of β- glucosidase is obtained in leukocytes.

Interpretation : In classical cases of Gaucher’s disease, a deficiency in beeta-glucosidase enzyme activity is a characteristic finding, with levels typically measuring before 15% of the mean normal. However in this indicidual inzyme activity of 117.3% of mean normal was obtained, which may suggest a late-onset form of the disease or carrier status. Therefore it is recommended to perform further clinical correlation to determine the patients condition accurately.

Recomendations –

  • It is suggested to confirm the enzyme deficiency from cultured skin fibroblasts.
  • GBA gene mutation analysis is recommended for identification of causative mutations, and / or carrier status and subsequent prenatal testing (testing facility is available at Sandor )
